newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark steady in Europe, awaits Germany's Ifo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark steady in Europe, awaits Germany's Ifo.

text.p: The dollar was steady to slightly weaker in morning Europe, holding above 1.79 marks ahead Germany's Ifo June survey but easier on the yen amid concerns of higher Japanese interest rates.
Dollar/yen drifted back below 116 yen overnight following Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) annual report said the country's economic recovery was close to self-sustaining.

"The EPA annual report was upbeat and the market has picked up on the comments that companies and individuals need to be aware of interest rates rising," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.
The EPA said the report was not pushing for a change in Bank of Japan monetary policy, and stressed the report was highlighting the fact that interest rates may rise one day.
Dealers said short-covering ahead of today's U.S. May trade numbers and the Japanese market's winding-down into a long, holiday weekend also served to add some pressure to dollar/yen.
By 0836 GMT, dollar/yen stood at 115.53/58 against 116.00/05 late Thursday in Europe. Mark/yen was also weaker, trading at 64.37/39 from 64.78/80 yen.
U.S. May trade data is expected to show a deficit of $9.2 billion from April's $8.4 billion shortfall.
European markets were focused on today's German research institute Ifo's business climate index for June due around 0800 GMT today. Analysts said average expectations are for a figure around 95.7.
A figure above here will lend the mark some support and may prompt a dollar/mark correction below key supports in the mid-1.78 mark region, said analysts.

"If the Ifo proves to be fairly soft, we're probably going to try to make another stab through 1.80," said a Japanese bank dealer. "But the market is still nervous above there and it may prove difficult to hold into the weekend."
By 0750 GMT, dollar/mark was trading at 1.7928/33 against 1.7920/25 marks late Thursday.
Bundesbank member Franz-Christoph Zeitler and German Finance Minister Theo Waigel are speaking today as is German Chancellor Helmut Kohl at 0930 GMT, adding to the cautious tone of the market today.

An EU monetary committee meeting is also scheduled for today amid speculation over the topics to be discussed, with many in the market looking for some attention being paid to the strength of the Irish punt within the ERM grid.
